title: _🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_
body:
_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Retain cross-file patterns when their anchor disappears.**

An explicit pattern can span files, but matching still derives identity from the current `finding.file` anchor. If `a.py:10` disappears from a pattern also reported at `b.py:20`, the matcher resolves the old record and creates a new record instead of recording partial progress.

- `lintro/ai/review/finding_matcher.py#L201-L204`: Match explicit multi-file occurrence patterns independently of the transient anchor file, or use normalized occurrence overlap to retain the prior record.
- `tests/unit/ai/review/test_finding_matcher.py#L528-L548`: Add a cross-file partial-progress case that asserts one carried record, no resolved record, and a total of two occurrences after `a.py:10` is fixed.

- `tests/unit/ai/review/test_finding_matcher.py#L528-L548`

</details>

title: _🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_
body:
_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Deduplicate occurrence locations before counting them.**

`parse_occurrences` preserves duplicate `file` and `line` pairs. The matcher uses the tuple length for `occurrences_total` and partial-progress counts. If the model reports `a.py:10` twice and later reports it once, state incorrectly shows one addressed occurrence although the same location remains.

Deduplicate validated occurrences while preserving their order. Add a regression test for repeated identical locations.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    return tuple(occurrence for occurrence in parsed if occurrence is not None)
+    return tuple(
+        dict.fromkeys(occurrence for occurrence in parsed if occurrence is not None),
+    )
```
</details>

As per PR objectives, occurrence totals must represent pattern-level locations.



<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
    parsed = (
        FindingOccurrence.from_dict(item) for item in value if isinstance(item, dict)
    )
    return tuple(
        dict.fromkeys(occurrence for occurrence in parsed if occurrence is not None),
    )
```

</details>

title: _🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_
body:
_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Prevent exact question references from using the same-file fallback.**

If `a.py:7` is a question and `a.py:42` is a finding, a reference to `a.py:7` filters out the question and returns `a.py:42` through `candidates[0]`. The summary then assigns unrelated severity to a question.

- `lintro/ai/review/verdict.py#L134-L138`: Check exact same-file matches before filtering questions. Return `None` when the exact location contains only questions. Keep the fallback only when no exact match exists.
- `tests/unit/ai/review/test_verdict.py#L198-L207`: Add a real finding at another line in `a.py` and assert that a reference to the question line still resolves to `None`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    candidates = [
-        finding
-        for finding in findings
-        if finding.file == path and not finding.is_question
-    ]
+    same_file = [finding for finding in findings if finding.file == path]
+    if line is not None:
+        exact = [finding for finding in same_file if finding.line == line]
+        if exact:
+            return next(
+                (finding for finding in exact if not finding.is_question),
+                None,
+            )
+    candidates = [finding for finding in same_file if not finding.is_question]
```
</details>



<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
    same_file = [finding for finding in findings if finding.file == path]
    if line is not None:
        exact = [finding for finding in same_file if finding.line == line]
        if exact:
            return next(
                (finding for finding in exact if not finding.is_question),
                None,
            )
    candidates = [finding for finding in same_file if not finding.is_question]
```

</details>
